description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing normal lung fields and mediastinal structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a posterior-anterior chest radiograph displaying clear lung fields without evidence of consolidation, effusion, or masses. The heart size appears within normal limits, and the mediastinal contours are unremarkable. The bony thoracic structures, including ribs and spine, show no obvious abnormalities. The diaphragm is well-defined bilaterally, and there is no visible air under the diaphragm.

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT scan showing bilateral pulmonary findings.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT scan demonstrates bilateral lung fields with areas of increased attenuation suggestive of patchy infiltrates. The mediastinum appears central, and no significant mediastinal shift is evident. The lung parenchyma shows abnormalities, including possible ground-glass opacities or consolidations. The scan is de-identified and does not include contrast enhancement.

description.short_caption: Histopathology of lung nodule biopsy showing granulomatous inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a lung tissue biopsy with granulomatous inflammation. The granulomas are composed of clusters of epithelioid macrophages and multinucleated giant cells, surrounded by lymphocytes. The background tissue appears fibrotic. No organisms are directly visible in this stain, but the findings are consistent with an infectious or inflammatory etiology. The stain type is likely hematoxylin and eosin (H&E).

description.short_caption: AFB stain showing acid-fast bacilli in lung nodule tissue.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast bacillus (AFB) stain of lung nodule tissue. The background tissue appears blue, while a single red, rod-shaped bacillus is visible in the center of the field, consistent with acid-fast organisms. The stain highlights the presence of mycobacteria against the tissue background.

description.short_caption: Histological section with a small organism stained in purple, highlighted by an arrow.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a histological section stained with a technique that highlights a small, purple-stained organism against a blue-green background. The organism is pointed out by a black arrow. The surrounding tissue appears to have a fibrous or cellular texture, with no other organisms clearly visible in this field. The stain and morphology suggest a focus on identifying a specific pathogen.
